notes: The prompt self-declares a turn-based JRPG with a party, a progression board, equipment and a combat loop, so RPG leads on the Turn-based RPG preset, and Adventure is named second for the story-driven pilgrimage whose chaptered-journey shape this build takes. I kept the preset's name and options but swapped its world-open shape, because the author's answer describes three handcrafted zones reached through a stylized world-map route that unlocks the next one, which is the opposite of one contiguous surface — that swap is what puts the build on P4, and since the prompt asks for separate zones rather than one map the usual one-continuous-map override does not apply; P4 is not a route running today, so it is flagged as deferred rather than silently collapsed to a single surface. Decided without a user: gate-progression carries the objective-based zone unlock, and I left Adventure's chapter-threshold and one-way-drop rows aside as duplicates of it, since separate zone maps already make backtracking impossible; I did not take building-interior, treating the dungeon and temple as zones in their own right rather than interior transitions off an outdoor map, so no P3; and collectible-nodes should read as treasure chests and ability items rather than RPG's mining veins. Two things with no home in this form: the save spheres that heal and save are Adventure's journey-save-point row, which the leading genre does not offer, and the blitzball-style side minigame is real content but sits outside the stated vertical slice, so no Sports genre or arena shape was taken for it — combat resolution, the sphere grid, cross-platform input and the audio and lighting direction are mechanics and presentation with no layout expression at all.
